title: Republic of Ireland Gender Pay Gap Report 2026
summary: Republic of Ireland Gender Pay Gap Report 2026
body_markdown:
At Diageo, inclusivity has long been central to who we are. We believe everyone deserves to work in an environment where they can thrive, where their contributions are equally valued, and where their uniqueness is both recognised and celebrated. Diageo believes an inclusive culture strengthens our business and supports long-term performance, while helping us deliver our purpose of crafting iconic drinks chosen for life’s moments.


In this report, we explain our pay gap, the factors influencing it and the actions we are taking. Our combined mean pay gap for the Republic of Ireland has decreased from +2.2% in 2025 to -1.6% in 2026. For our three entities within the Republic of Ireland, the 2026 mean pay gaps are: Diageo Ireland -3.5%, R&A Bailey & Co +5.7%, Guinness Storehouse -7.1%. While we are proud of the progress we are making in this area, we recognise there is still work to be done, and Diageo is committed to achieving its goals in eliminating the pay gap across our workforce.


We remain focused on strengthening gender balance across our business and investing in the next generation of female leaders, particularly in areas where women have historically been underrepresented. Globally, we continue to work towards our ambition of 50% representation of women in leadership roles by 2030, while continuing to build a diverse and inclusive workforce. In Ireland, female representation across our leadership population increased from 53.1% in FY25 to 56.3% in FY26. These results reflect our continued focus on strengthening female representation and building a strong pipeline of female talent.


As a global business, our success depends on attracting, developing and retaining talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. We believe there is power in bringing together different perspectives and experiences, helping us better reflect the consumers and communities we serve. Here in Ireland, home to some of our most iconic brands and a proud heritage, we are committed to creating a workplace where everyone has the opportunity to contribute, develop and perform at their best. While we are encouraged by the progress outlined in this year’s Gender Pay Gap Report, we know there is more to do. We remain committed to improving gender balance, developing diverse talent pipelines and ensuring everyone at Diageo has the opportunity to grow and thrive, equally.
